transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been having a really hard time lately. We got a new operations manager at work, and ever since he started, he's been picking apart the inspection procedures I've used for years. I just... I can't seem to leave work at work anymore. I come home completely wound up, I snap at my husband over nothing, and I just lie awake at night replaying meetings in my head. And then the next day, I end up second-guessing routine quality calls that I used to make without any trouble. It's just really getting to me.
Did these feelings of being wound up and anxious start only after your new operations manager began, or were you experiencing similar worry and tension even before he started?

No, I was doing completely fine before he came in. The trouble really started building within just a few weeks of him making changes to our procedures. And... well, by the second month he was there, I knew my reactions to him were affecting me well beyond the workday.
Besides feeling anxious and wound up, have you also been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or down. It's really just the stress and feeling so keyed up all the time. I still want to do the things I normally enjoy, I just... well, sometimes it's hard to fully focus on them because my mind is still back at the plant. But no, I haven't been feeling depressed or anything like that.

Aside from the situation at work, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other areas of your life too—like your health, finances, or family—or does the worry stay focused mainly on the work issues?

No, it's really just work. I mean, sure, everyone worries a little about money or their health sometimes, but nothing out of the ordinary for me. It's just... the stuff with the new manager. That's what's keeping me up at night. My husband and my health and everything else are fine. It's just that one thing that's completely throwing me off.
Would you say this stress has noticeably affected your ability to perform your job duties or has caused significant strain in your relationship with your husband?

Yes, it definitely has. At work, my record has taken a hit lately. I've missed some internal deadlines, and... well, I've been pulling back from meetings I'm expected to attend. It's just getting too hard to deal with. 

And at home, yeah, it's causing problems there too. My husband and I are arguing a lot more than normal. I'm just not keeping up with our usual evening routines the way I used to, I guess because I'm just so wrapped up in all this stress.
Is the situation with your new manager still ongoing right now, or has anything changed or resolved with that since it started?

No, it's still very much ongoing. I still have to report to him every day, and we're still using the new procedures he put in place. So... the situation hasn't ended at all. It's not like the problem was fixed and I just kept stressing about it for months afterward. The cause of the stress is still right there, every time I clock in.
